description: Which of a receiving school's published equivalencies point to courses its own catalog does not hold? Every published (direct) CourseAtlas equivalency into one receiving school, read by sending school, each receiving course looked up in the school's learning units at this publish through the transfer check's own course join, and each rule put in exactly one class: held_current (held in the current catalog), held_retired (held only as an archived course; the last edition it was seen in is given), likely_renumbered (not held, but a current course has the same number with another prefix, or a title that matches once roman numerals, punctuation and the words I, II and Introduction are set aside; that course is named), generic_credit (the receiving course publishes a credit range; reported, not a defect) or not_held. A rule with several receiving courses takes the class of its least held one. For each likely_renumbered rule, the checklists that require the named course are counted. The answer: a summary of counts per class, then one row per rule outside held_current and generic_credit, sorted by checklists affected, highest first, each with its CourseAtlas source_url, and every read as a step with its count and ms. A call reads until its time is spent and answers with `continue.arguments` to send back as they are; the counts carry across calls, the rows are each call's own. Read-only: it changes no rule, playlist or catalog row. Recognition is the school's act; findings are for the school to confirm. Each row names its current FORM's wording source: source_url, capture_file, catalog_year and source_catalog_name are that one source's, never the record's whole span. A row whose record holds more than one form or more than one source also carries version_count, source_count, first_edition_seen and last_edition_seen, and one sentence saying so in words; a record with one form and one source carries none of them and reads exactly as it always has. The forms themselves, each with its own content and its own sources, come from the one-record get, never from a list.

carried.description: Set by `continue.arguments`: where the reading stopped and the counts so far, sent back unchanged

limit.description: Optional: the findings listed (default 20, at most 100)

sender_unitid.description: Optional: one sending school's IPEDS UNITID, to read only its rules

unitid.description: The receiving school's IPEDS UNITID, e.g. 216764

name: equivalency_audit

continue.description: When more remains to read: the arguments for the next call; null when the school is read

rows.description: This call's rules outside held_current and generic_credit: sending_school, sending_course, equivalency_id, approved, revised, receiving (each course as published with its own class), class, candidate, checklists_affected, source_url

summary.description: counts per class, rules_read, sending_schools_read, sending_schools, out_of_date, learning_units_looked_up - every call so far

title: Equivalency Audit
